display.title: Rosh Hashanah, the Head of the Year
display.summary_short: Why our Sages call it Rosh Hashanah, the 'head' of the year: like the head of the body, it shapes every day that follows. Plus the machzor, the laws, and hearing the shofar.
display.summary_long: A short holiday talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, aired days before Rosh Hashanah 5753. Uncle Yossi explains that our Sages did not call the day 'the beginning of the year' but Rosh Hashanah, 'the head of the year'. Just as every part of the body depends on the head, and a healthy head means a healthy body, the way we behave on the two days of Rosh Hashanah affects the whole year. To behave properly we need to know the laws and customs: use a machzor with the special Rosh Hashanah prayers, review the laws in the Shulchan Aruch, and be in shul on time to hear the shofar on both days. As we hear the shofar, we pray to soon hear the great shofar announcing Moshiach.
display.lesson: Spend Rosh Hashanah properly, because it is the head that sets the tone for the whole year.

date.note: Shofar 'this coming Monday, September 28th, and Tuesday, September 29th' = Rosh Hashanah 5753; aired the Tuesday before.
